title: Chinese envoys visit Funan
description: Envoys of the Chinese state of Wu visit Funan, and their reports are the earliest written account of a state in the Mekong delta.

title: Isanapura becomes the capital of Chenla
description: King Isanavarman I rules from Isanapura, whose brick temples are the largest surviving group from before Angkor.

title: Jayavarman II declared universal monarch
description: Jayavarman II is consecrated as universal monarch on Mount Kulen, the traditional start of the Khmer Empire.

title: Yasodharapura founded
description: Yasovarman I comes to the throne and builds a new capital at Angkor, which stays the centre of the empire for five centuries.

title: Capital moved to Koh Ker
description: Jayavarman IV rules from Koh Ker, where he builds a seven-tiered pyramid, until the court returns to Angkor in 944.

title: Banteay Srei consecrated
description: The small red sandstone temple, built by a court official rather than a king, is dedicated to Shiva.

title: Angkor Wat built
description: The temple built for Suryavarman II, the largest religious monument in the world, is largely finished around the time of his death.

title: Cham sack of Angkor
description: A Cham fleet sails up the Mekong and the Tonlé Sap, takes the Khmer capital and kills the king.

title: Jayavarman VII crowned
description: After driving out the Chams, Jayavarman VII takes the throne and builds Angkor Thom, the Bayon and a network of roads and hospitals.

title: Zhou Daguan arrives at Angkor
description: A Chinese envoy begins a stay of almost a year at the Khmer court, and his account is the only surviving eyewitness description of Angkor.

title: Capital moved to Phnom Penh
description: After the fall of Angkor, King Ponhea Yat settles the court at the meeting of the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers.

title: Fall of Longvek
description: A Siamese army under Naresuan takes the Cambodian capital, after which the kingdom is dominated by its neighbours.

title: Ang Duong crowned
description: Ang Duong is crowned under the joint suzerainty of Siam and Vietnam after their war over Cambodia.

title: Henri Mouhot visits Angkor
description: The French naturalist's published journal makes the ruins of Angkor widely known in Europe.

title: French protectorate established
description: King Norodom signs a treaty placing Cambodia under French protection, which lasts for ninety years.

title: Battambang and Siem Reap returned
description: Siam cedes the western provinces, including Angkor, to French Indochina by treaty.

title: Sihanouk becomes king
description: The French choose the eighteen-year-old Norodom Sihanouk as king; he dominates Cambodian politics for the next half century.

title: Independence from France
description: France hands over its remaining powers and Cambodia becomes independent under King Sihanouk.

title: Preah Vihear awarded to Cambodia
description: The International Court of Justice rules that the temple on the Thai border belongs to Cambodia.

title: American bombing begins
description: The United States begins the secret bombing of Vietnamese communist bases inside Cambodia, known as Operation Menu.

title: Sihanouk overthrown
description: The National Assembly removes Sihanouk as head of state and Lon Nol takes power, drawing Cambodia into the Vietnam War.

title: Fall of Phnom Penh
description: The Khmer Rouge take the capital and order its two million people into the countryside.

title: Cambodian genocide
description: Under Pol Pot between 1.5 and 2 million people, about a quarter of the population, die from execution, forced labour, hunger and disease.

title: Paris Peace Agreements
description: The warring Cambodian factions and nineteen countries sign a settlement that ends the civil war and puts the country under a United Nations transitional authority.

title: United Nations-run election
description: Almost ninety per cent of registered voters take part in an election organised by the United Nations, which the royalist party FUNCINPEC wins.

title: Monarchy restored
description: A new constitution makes Cambodia a constitutional monarchy and Sihanouk becomes king again.

title: Hun Sen ousts Ranariddh
description: Forces loyal to Hun Sen defeat those of his co-prime minister Norodom Ranariddh, leaving Hun Sen in sole control.

title: Death of Pol Pot
description: The former Khmer Rouge leader dies under house arrest by his own movement, which collapses within the year.

title: First Khmer Rouge tribunal verdict
description: The joint Cambodian and United Nations tribunal convicts Kang Kek Iew, head of the S-21 prison, of crimes against humanity.

title: Main opposition party dissolved
description: The Supreme Court dissolves the Cambodia National Rescue Party, and the ruling party wins every seat at the next election.
